title: Recognition Complexity of M-Identifiability in Sparse Factor Models with Bounded Latent Degree
banked_reason: The proposal promised a resolution of ordinary M-ID recognition, but that classification remains open; the sound structural remainder is incremental and below the field floor.
gap_reasons: The proposal promised a resolution of ordinary M-ID recognition (a sound-and-complete polynomial recognizer or an NP-completeness proof), but this node explicitly leaves that classification open; Sturma et al., arXiv:2502.02986v2 §5, Conjecture 5.3, is therefore still the unresolved target.

The proposed 3-SAT upgrade supplies no gadget, encoding invariant, recursive completion, reverse-direction proof, or unintended-witness exclusion lemma and merely restates the original unresolved bottleneck.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived an exact cut normal form, a deterministic O(n log n) recognizer for maximum latent degree three, a sharp degree-four failure of singleton peeling, and a bounded-incidence-treewidth FPT result.  It did not produce either a complete unrestricted endpoint optimizer or a verified NP-hardness reduction with recursive completion, so Conjecture 5.3 and the proposal's promised unrestricted classification remain open.
tldr: Ordinary M-ID recognition remains open in general. The local witness condition has an exact joint-parent cut normal form, and ordinary witnesses collapse to singleton witnesses when every latent has at most three children. Residual child and child-pair counts then give deterministic \(O(n\log n)\) full recognition with replayable certificates. An explicit degree-four graph needs a size-two first witness, so the singleton threshold is sharp; bounded incidence treewidth gives a separate fixed-parameter route. Local endpoint-selection complexity, degree-four recognition, and Conjecture 5.3 for unrestricted recursive M-ID remain open.
gap: The published two-flow verifier handles fixed endpoint sets and its bounded-witness recognizer does not classify unrestricted endpoint selection or full recursive ordinary M-ID.
fill: Investigate the exact joint-parent endpoint-selection language through a cut normal form; prove a polynomial optimizer or a hardness reduction valid for full recursive completion. Establish that the genuine ordinary size-one criterion suffices at maximum latent degree three, that degree four is the first level where this restriction can fail, and that bounded incidence treewidth admits a structural route.
